approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including an aromatic nitrogen/carbon exchange that preserves molecular formula. After normalizing identities and rejecting duplicates, it submits the first complete batch allowed by its short-term memory of inverse local motif changes. It moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that move worsens the current score, using canonical text order for exact score ties. A separate best-observed archive keeps its own score and canonical tie rule.
approach.novelty: Among equally best accepted neighbors, choose the one whose local motif counts differ most from the current molecule, then use canonical order if that structural comparison also ties. The distance accounts for motif multiplicity and normalizes by the combined motif counts. This gives an equally scored change in local chemical environments priority over canonical spelling and may expose a different next neighborhood. The earlier tie-selection siblings preferred fewer heavy atoms; this rule can choose smaller, equal-sized or larger graphs. It reuses the Parent's existing motifs without changing the generation or tabu rules and adds no history policy.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-abcd951ab7cc retains the repaired inverse-motif graph walk and its direct aromatic nitrogen relocation, with complete three-replica macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population deviation 0.006329100643035156. Its actual per-seed summary.json and run.log files report successful completion. The lexical tie rule sometimes chooses a neighbor that preserves more of the source's local motif profile despite an equally scored accepted maximum with greater local structural change. A passive audit joins all 4350 accepted records to their emitted proposal counts, source states and scored trajectories and reproduces all 435 selected transitions. There are 409 unique maxima and 26 exact maximum ties containing 64 candidates; 16 tie sets have unequal normalized motif distances from their source. Maximum source-distance selection would change nine lexical winners: seven source-score plateaus, one improving maximum and one worsening maximum, across five task/replica sessions in three tasks. Every changed choice increases the registered distance at identical accepted score. Two occur in terminal batches and provide no subsequent proposal opportunity. Across the nine choices, the selected graph has fewer heavy atoms than the lexical winner once, equal size four times and greater size four times. This is a distinct structural-change preference rather than a size preference. Siblings n-770a3cefca6a and n-d4f4384cd477 both implemented minimum-heavy-atom tie resolution and report the same panel scores and paired loss -0.0011038146568116785; their matching records are not independent performance replication. They establish exercised tie choices but no size-based score benefit. The source-distance audit has 277308 passing checks and is retained in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-06-improve-L16.plan-audit.json with source/log/trajectory receipts. Its passive full-selected-history comparator changes no winner relative to source-only distance, so the proposed mechanism does not add historical memory. These saved-batch comparisons reveal available choices, not scores for alternative continuations.
hypothesis: Among exact accepted-score batch maxima, select the neighbor with greatest multiset-Jaccard distance between its inherited radius-one motif occurrence counts and the current source's counts, then use canonical lexical order for any remaining tie.

finding_summary.headline: Motif-distance ties changed 20 walk states, but the panel score fell
finding_summary.insights: The experiment rules out failure to exercise the selector: it changed real, scored next states and was followed by 600 later accepted proposals after removing overlap between the recorded histories. It also shows why larger local structural steps are insufficient evidence of more useful exploration. The extra plateau profiles came with extra plateau moves, and longer equal-score episodes still appeared. Twenty later archive gains occurred in the affected continuations, compared with 26 in the corresponding recorded parent histories, but the overlapping paths prevent assigning a causal gain to each tie choice. The rule sometimes chose smaller molecules and sometimes larger ones. The molecular assessment finds that some equally scored differences introduce reactive attachments or unusual sulfur connectivity, while conventional ring and carbonyl families remain available. Greater distance between local motif counts therefore supplies neither compactness nor chemical plausibility. The direct selection mechanism is confirmed; its proposed overall score benefit is refuted on this panel. What remains open is whether a distance that distinguishes useful structural alternatives from score-insensitive local decoration can improve later search; this experiment does not settle that broader question.
finding_summary.results: Twenty choices among equally best accepted molecules changed the next walk state, and all 20 increased exact motif distance from the current molecule without giving up the accepted maximum score. Eighteen occurred at the same score as the source, one during an improving move and one during a worsening move. Nineteen choices had actual continuations; one was terminal. The rule encountered 40 exact maximum ties, compared with 26 in the parent, while preserving canonical fallback and the original feedback, archive and memory rules. Plateau episodes contained 60 equal-score moves, each visiting a distinct motif profile within its episode, compared with 49 such moves in the parent. Coverage per move was unchanged, and the longest plateau grew from six moves to nine. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519947, a paired loss of 0.001812 against the required gain of 0.002. One seed improved slightly and two declined. Only deco_hop endpoints changed; the other four task endpoints were identical in every seed.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aryl/carbonyl families coexist with reactive attachments, oversized decorations and undefined sulfur cages
molecular.overall_character: Node n-4341f3da1e57 was assessed from all supplied trajectories for all five tasks and all three seeds; the digest has no tasks_without_trajectories. Each task contains 900 evaluated records, including 870 optimizer proposals. The proposals are branched, ring-rich molecules: every task has string-level ring_closure_rate 1.0, while aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.7184 to 1.0. These are presence counters, not aromatic atom fractions. Charged and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0 throughout. The chemical range includes comparatively conventional fused aromatic amides, decorated oxo/thioxo azaheterocycles, aryl compounds carrying primary and cyclic amines, bridged N/O lactams, and densely connected fluorinated sulfur cages. Diversity is moderate across these families but the displayed leaders repeatedly vary the same local frameworks. Rings, aromatic groups, carbonyls and amines are already accessible. The recurring deficiencies are stable heteroatom connectivity, economical substitution, and defined feasible stereochemistry. Many leading sulfur-rich graphs have weak synthetic credibility, although some indole amides have recognizable conventional chemistry. Passive parsing with the supplied RDKit 2023.09.6 environment succeeded for every supplied child and parent trajectory molecule. All atom, ring and functional-bond counts below are derived directly from those observed graphs; ring counts use toolkit perception and do not certify geometry or synthesis. The passive descriptors, input hashes and comparison receipts are in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-06-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json, produced by the adjacent molecular-audit.py. Relative to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, every replica retains the same best molecular identity set on four tasks. The changed best identities are confined to deco_hop, whose chemistry is described below. This is an output comparison, with no judgement about mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer proposals contain 21–29 heavy atoms, median 25, and 2–6 perceived rings. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9563. The leading family places an aryl amide or aryl ketone on a fused indole, benzofuran or benzothiophene, with alkoxy, methyl, amino, thiol and halo substituents. The maximum-scoring benzofuran has 26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings, but also an N-chloroamide and a chlorinated amino-bearing carbon. The 23-heavy-atom indole carboxanilide at 0.39905049777278273 is a comparatively conventional molecular framework. Later examples include partially dearomatized, bridged N/S systems; the final displayed proposal scores 0.3852230774700024 and retains a sulfur-containing bridge and an N–N bond. The parent has the same best identities and scores in every seed.
liabilities: The best benzofuran couples otherwise recognizable medicinal fragments to an N–Cl bond and a chlorinated amino-bearing carbon, which raise stability concerns. N-halogen bonds occur in 169 of 870 proposals.

N–O/N–F combinations, free thiols and multiply connected sulfur environments recur. The ordinary indole amide demonstrates that this chemistry is not uniformly implausible, but a valid graph does not settle the more unusual products.
The displayed bridged products lack assigned stereochemistry; increased ring connectivity alone provides no evidence of a realizable geometry.
missing_features: The stronger aromatic/carbonyl arrangement has limited representation as chemically conventional matched donor/acceptor placements in the displayed leaders; several alternatives instead carry reactive attachments or distorted ring frameworks.
Defined configurations and demonstrably feasible alternatives to the late bridged frameworks are absent. These trajectories do not identify a unique missing pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy, fluorophenyl indole amide scores 0.3051048083696145; the displayed conventional indole amide reaches 0.39905049777278273 and the N-chlorinated benzofuran reaches 0.41003927643747895. A heavily modified indole whose amide carbonyl is replaced by a branched amino-bearing linkage scores 0.03343008011310944, while a ring-expanded, partly nonaromatic carbonyl compound scores 0.021532846118034143. These comparisons associate the intact compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement with stronger scores, without isolating any single required substituent. The displayed chloro and bromo bridged amide analogues both score 0.3900523103411983, so the observed score does not distinguish those halogen identities in that local context.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 30–55 heavy atoms, median 40, and 2–7 perceived rings; all contain aromatic tokens. Fused oxo/thioxo azaheterocycles and substituted aryl groups persist while aminoalkyl, imine, ether, haloalkyl and sulfur-bearing appendages expand. The maximum-scoring molecule has 52 heavy atoms, three perceived rings, six sulfur atoms and 18 toolkit-counted rotatable bonds. It includes a carbon–sulfur triple bond followed by another sulfur, a sulfur–chlorine bond and additional sulfur–carbon multiple bonding. The final displayed seed instead has a decorated fused heterocycle, cyclic ether, branched alkyl substituents and a disulfide. These large structures contain ordinary fragments, but the leading connectivity is synthetically questionable. All replica-best identity sets differ from the parent. For seed 0 the parent maximum is 0.6161710037174721, with 51 heavy atoms and three sulfur atoms; the child maximum is 0.6087622549019608, with 52 heavy atoms and six sulfur atoms. Across all proposals, sulfur triple-bond incidence is 110/870 in the child versus 1/870 in the parent. Late proposals, evaluations 201–300 pooled across seeds, average 44.60666666666667 heavy atoms versus 43.44 in the parent. This describes the changed output without assigning the score difference to a particular bond.
liabilities: Neutral carbon–sulfur triple bonds with additional sulfur connectivity are a major plausibility concern. Sulfur–halogen bonds occur in 307 of 870 proposals, including the sulfur–chlorine group in the maximum-scoring example.

Long, heavily branched side chains, imines, haloalkyl substituents and multiple sulfur functionalities create substantial chemical and conformational complexity. The maximum-scoring molecule has five potential tetrahedral centres flagged by RDKit and none assigned.

A retained aromatic heterocycle does not establish synthetic feasibility for the surrounding attachments; the less exotic carbon-alkyne counterpart already has the same observed score as its sulfur-triple-bond relative.
missing_features: Compact matched versions of the useful heterocycle/aryl attachment pattern remain underrepresented among the leaders, even though observed equal-score variants show that some appendage growth and sulfur substitution are dispensable locally.
Stable, stereochemically defined linker and peripheral-group alternatives are incomplete. The available scores do not reveal a uniquely required missing scaffold or decoration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial ester/phenol-decorated fused dione scores 0.548381482770623; a displayed ring-reorganized relative scores 0.526081691583997, while the heavily decorated leading family reaches 0.6087622549019608. The visible ascent retains the heterocycle/aryl combination while changing its attachments, rather than simply increasing aromatic or ring content. Within that family, the 51- and 53-heavy-atom aminoalkyl variants both score 0.6085506367495452. A matched carbon-alkyne and sulfur-triple-bond pair both score 0.6076189311483429. Thus those particular extra atoms and unusual sulfur bonding have no demonstrated local score advantage. The final displayed cyclic-ether/disulfide family includes 0.5886256141800983 and a further ring-reorganized proposal at 0.5626123811970203.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 32–43 heavy atoms, median 36, and 2–9 perceived rings. Aromatic-token presence is 1.0 and halogen presence is 0.9966. Higher-scoring molecules combine phenolic or halogenated aryl groups with primary aminomethyl groups and cyclic/tertiary amines, embedded in bridged sulfur heterocycles or small nitrogen rings. The maximum-scoring graph has 32 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings and five perceived rings overall, including an S–S double-bond bridge. Another leading family includes an aziridine, an amino-substituted nitrogen ring and a sulfur–sulfur double-bond attachment. The low-scoring early family is richer in carboxylic acid, amide and sulfonamide functionality. All child trajectories and best identities are identical to the parent on this task.
liabilities: S–S multiple bonds occur in 336 of 870 proposals, and the maximum-scoring graph retains one. Other leaders contain sulfur–carbon multiple bonding combined with additional sulfur substitution.

The small nitrogen rings and dense heteroatom bridges raise strain and reactivity concerns. All 870 proposals have potential tetrahedral centres flagged by RDKit, while the digest stereocentre-token rate is 0.0.
Aryl halogens and amines are recognizable medicinal chemistry, but their presence does not resolve the unusual sulfur valence and unspecified configurations of the complete products.
missing_features: Primary and cyclic amines are already present. The leading sample lacks a convincing set of ordinary, stereochemically defined frameworks preserving their observed spacing from the aryl groups without the sulfur bridges or small-ring liabilities.

The molecular records provide neither an established protonation state nor a validated three-dimensional arrangement. No additional specific amine ring or target contact can be inferred from these scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: A displayed acid/amide/sulfonamide aryl compound scores 0.007468397818197266, whereas the aryl/amine/sulfur families reach 0.8856242185485628 and 0.9148143511682032. The visible direction associates amine-bearing aryl arrangements and loss of the earlier acid-rich architecture with stronger scores; it does not establish a binding pose or measured basicity. In a close pair, removing the methylene separating a ring nitrogen from the attached sulfur heterocycle changes 0.8663008496126992 to 0.3331237338421948. A related replacement that removes aromatic character from one aryl ring scores 0.04252669549740123. Conversely, carbon-versus-sulfur variants within the bridged framework both score 0.8825461379136246. Linker placement and aromatic organization matter locally, while the unusual sulfur identity is not always distinguished.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 27–45 heavy atoms, median 35, and 3–8 perceived rings; every proposal contains aromatic tokens. The leading family is a bridged phenyl/azaaryl polycycle containing an N-methyl lactam, unsaturation, alkyl substituents and an N–O bridge. The maximum-scoring member has 31 heavy atoms and formula C26H31N3O2. Related leaders replace tether carbons with nitrogen or insert an additional oxygen. Lower-scoring examples include ring-opened carbonyl chains and heavily brominated sulfur/N–N systems; the displayed final seed has larger sulfur-containing N/O polycycles. O-halogen bonds occur in 215 of 870 proposals; a displayed low-scoring brominated molecule contains an O–Br bond alongside unusual substituted sulfur and N–N connectivity.
The multiply bridged lactam and later larger sulfur cages lack assigned stereochemistry. The maximum-scoring graph has three potential tetrahedral centres flagged by RDKit.

Assigned configurations and demonstrated geometric feasibility for the bridged cores are absent. The limited gradient does not identify a uniquely required new functional group.

The displayed open carbonyl-chain relatives score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515 despite retaining substantial aromatic content. The displayed leaders are compact, densely bridged fluorinated sulfur/aza cages containing carbonyls and NH groups; the maximum-scoring graph has 30 heavy atoms, five sulfur atoms, three fluorines and six perceived rings. The sulfur-linked hydroxyfluoromethyl group and the final N-fluoro/aldehyde-containing cages add stability concerns to already constrained frameworks. N-halogen bonds occur in 288 of 870 proposals and sulfur triple bonds in 91 of 870.

Successful parsing and compact heavy-atom count do not establish a feasible cage geometry or a practical synthesis. Closely related sulfur-rich structures can have very low scores as well as high ones.

Matched conventional ring and linker alternatives preserving those polar-group positions remain unshown among the leaders. These observations do not establish a specific absent pharmacophore, nor an absolute aromaticity requirement.

These large differences across related frameworks make precise carbonyl placement, composition and connectivity more defensible readings than a blanket preference for sulfur or more rings; the rows do not isolate the individual objective components.

A conventional indole amide reaches 0.39905049777278273. A matched carbon-alkyne/sulfur-triple-bond pair shares 0.6076189311483429, and carbon/sulfur ring variants share 0.8825461379136246. These observed equalities do not show a local score benefit from the unusual sulfur bonds.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make conventional matched heteroatom and linker replacements accessible while preserving the useful aryl, amine and carbonyl attachment pattern. Distinguish ordinary sulfur groups and carbon-bound halogens from heteroatom-halogen bonds and multiply connected sulfur; use actual feedback to establish which replacements retain useful scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The 51- and 53-heavy-atom aminoalkyl variants share 0.6085506367495452. The leading decorated heterocycle has 52 heavy atoms, six sulfur atoms and 18 rotatable bonds. A displayed 40-heavy-atom sulfur/N/O polycycle scores 0.1877368016216444, below the 31-heavy-atom bridged lactam at 0.21196904390980506. These are observed local examples, not a universal size-score relation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply economical peripheral chemistry alongside increasingly large decorated frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include coherent matched simplifications of branches, flexible appendages and unnecessary heteroatom connections while preserving the principal framework and polar-group attachments. Retain smaller alternatives when observed feedback supports them; do not presume that either growth or indiscriminate deletion improves chemistry and score together.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Deleting the methylene between a nitrogen and its attached sulfur heterocycle changes an observed score from 0.8663008496126992 to 0.3331237338421948. Open carbonyl-chain relatives score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515, while the constrained aryl/lactam family reaches 0.21196904390980506. Replacing a carbonyl oxygen with imino nitrogen in a close cage pair changes 0.519850349488241 to 0.48440391849409126.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically conventional ring and linker alternatives preserving the useful arrangement of aromatic and polar groups remain incomplete.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide matched variations in ring size, tether length and polar-group identity that preserve the other observed structural relationships. Expand access to ordinary feasible ring frameworks carrying the same useful attachment pattern, so chemical simplification can be explored without simultaneously erasing aromaticity, carbonyl placement and linker spacing.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The leading bridged lactam has three potential tetrahedral centres flagged by RDKit, the leading fluorinated sulfur cage has seven, and its displayed final cage has eleven; none is assigned. Small rings, multiply bridged N/O systems and unsaturated sulfur bridges recur among the supplied molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemical identity and geometric feasibility remain undefined for the constrained molecules the generator emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve feasible configurations where stereogenic relationships exist, and provide less constrained matched ring alternatives. Establish geometric plausibility for heavily bridged products rather than treating aromatic perception, ring closure or a successful molecular parse as evidence of a realizable three-dimensional molecule. The observed scores alone do not establish a stereochemical preference.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
